test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Identify the group of states that is a part of Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (As of June 2022).
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (GKRA) was launched by the Government of India on **20 June 2020** to address the economic challenges faced by migrant workers returning home during the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• The scheme focuses on creating livelihood opportunities and developing durable rural infrastructure in **116 districts across six states**, including Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand.
 
• Along with Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand, the other participating states are Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and Rajasthan.
 
• The initiative aligns with the government's objective to provide employment through **25 categories of public works**, such as rural housing, sanitation, road construction, and water conservation.
 
• The scheme was allocated an initial funding of **₹50,000 crore** to create immediate employment opportunities and support rural development in affected regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objective of GKRA:**

 
 
• The primary aim is to provide immediate employment to migrant workers and create durable rural infrastructure.
 
• The scheme integrates existing government programs such as MGNREGA, PMGSY, and Jal Jeevan Mission to expedite development.
 
 
 
• **Targeted Districts:**
 
 
• The 116 districts were selected based on data showing high concentrations of returning migrant workers.
 
• These districts span across six states, including Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• The Ministry of Rural Development spearheads the program with support from 12 other central ministries.
 
• Local panchayats were involved in mapping returning workers to ensure efficient targeting of benefits.
 
 
 
• **Skill Development:**
 
 
• GKRA focuses on skill development for workers to enhance their employability in the long term.
 
• The scheme seeks to build capacities in areas like construction, agriculture, and allied sectors.
 
 
 
• **COVID-19 Context:**
 
 
• The pandemic caused a massive reverse migration of workers from urban to rural areas, necessitating immediate livelihood interventions.
 
• GKRA served as a critical measure to mitigate the socioeconomic impact of the pandemic in rural India.
